affected_boundaries: verified directory scope and current source inputs

observed_behavior: Adding an untracked source file inside a verified Git directory scope left its certificate fresh.
expected_behavior: New untracked source inputs inside the verified scope invalidate the certificate.
causal_mechanism: Git diff compares tracked content. A directory can exist at the verified revision while new untracked files beneath it remain invisible to both working-tree and index diffs.

anti_pattern.structural_description: A tracked-content comparison is used as a complete enumeration of current directory inputs.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: New source files may affect execution without changing tracked files.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Freshness covers tracked changes and newly introduced nonignored files in the declared scope.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Alongside Git diffs, query Git ls-files for untracked nonignored scoped paths; fail closed on query errors.

applicability_conditions: A verification scope includes a tracked directory.
A new nonignored source file appears inside that scope.
known_non_matches: Changes outside the declared scope do not invalidate scoped proof.
confirmation_evidence: The focused real-Git test passed before introducing a scoped untracked file, then incorrectly returned fresh; removing the file restores freshness. The same test passes after adding the Git untracked-file query.
regression_proofs: tests/obligations.test.ts: real Git freshness detects committed, staged, unstaged and missing inputs while allowing unrelated changes
